title: Shadow Observables of Spinning Braneworld Black Holes
content: The apparent shape of the shadow cast by a black hole encodes its mass, spin, inclination, and any charge or tidal deformation without reference to the surrounding astrophysical environment. Starting from the Carter separability of null geodesics in Boyer--Lindquist coordinates, we derive the celestial coordinates $(\alpha,\beta)$ of the shadow boundary from first principles via a local tetrad computation, obtain the critical impact parameters $(\xi,\eta)$ that trace the photon ring, and define the Hioki--Maeda observables $(\mathcal{R}_s, \mathcal{D}_s)$ precisely. We prove three monotonicity theorems: the shadow radius $\mathcal{R}_s$ is strictly decreasing in the dimensionless spin $a/M$ at fixed inclination $\theta_0 = \pi/2$; the distortion $\mathcal{D}_s$ is strictly increasing in $a/M$; and for the braneworld Kerr geometry, $\mathcal{R}_s$ is strictly increasing in the tidal charge $Q$. These results establish that the map $(a/M,\theta_0)\mapsto(\mathcal{R}_s,\mathcal{D}_s)$ is locally invertible, providing the theoretical foundation for extracting the spin and inclination from shadow images. We compute shadow angular diameters for Sgr~$\mathrm{A}^{*}$ and M87$^{*}$ across a range of $a/M$ and $Q/M^{2}$, compare them with Event Horizon Telescope sensitivity, and discuss prospects for next-generation arrays. The Killing--Yano origin of the Carter constant and its role in Liouville integrability are treated explicitly, as is the BPS limit of charged braneworld black holes.
